summary: Tome I of Delambre and Méchain (1806) prints the station registers (Observations géodésiques, pp. 1-509) station by station from Dunkerque south to Montjoui. Each station gives the signal, the eccentric stand (r and y), the zenith distances, and for each angle the repeated series with the number of repetitions, the circle (D., F., B. n° 1 or n° 4 in the north) and a Résumé: reduction to centre, mean, reduction to the horizon and the value kept. The north part (Dunkerque to Rodez) is Delambre's; the south part (Rodez to Montjoui) is Méchain's and prints angles in grades with degrees beside them. The value kept is the one fixed by the special commission; the Tableau des triangles (pp. 513-542) gives it for each triangle angle with the register page. This file transcribes the registers of 96 stations and every triangle angle that has a register series.

stations.name: Jonquières
stations.occupied: 22 July 1792 (zenith distance of Clermont); 27 September 1793 (angles Coivrel-Clermont and Coivrel-Saint-Christophe); other series not dated

stations.signal: In 1740 the mill was the signal; in 1792 it gave no safe point. Delambre's signal was a triangular pyramid 3 toises high, faces covered with straw (dH = 2.25 toises); its centre was 7 toises from the centre of the mill, at an angle of 251° 7' 5" with Dammartin. A stake was driven at the centre and covered with earth; it was found again fifteen months later. In 1793 the wind had destroyed the signal, so Coivrel observed the miller's chimney and reduced it to the signal (SP = 7.3333 toises, CS = 16.771 toises; SC seen from Coivrel subtends 4' 29.34").

stations.signal: Belfry of the Collégiale, as in 1740. Delambre was warned it would soon be pulled down, and it was some months later; so he began the operation with the stations around it instead of going straight to Dunkerque. The instrument had its own scaffold, apart from the observer's, but still shook when the foot screws were touched. dH = 5.5556 toises.

stations.signal: The sighting point was the cap (calotte) of the lantern that then ended the dome of the Panthéon. When the observers came back to Paris in winter, the top of the lantern had been pulled down. They stood in the lower part that remained; the telescope was 1.431 toises above the last stair step. From Rondelet's plans the cap rose 4.85 toises above the last step, plus about 0.17 toise of thickness; dH = 3.5 toises.

stations.name: Bellassise
stations.occupied: 4 September 1792 (first visit, ended by Delambre's arrest); 9 to 13 October 1792 (return to put the Panthéon in place of the Invalides)
stations.signal: Middle pavilion of the château of Bellassise, chosen because the people of Montjai refused a signal on their ruined tower (used in 1670 and 1740), and because that tower could not be seen from the Invalides. The pavilion is a truncated four-sided pyramid with an upper base one toise square. The observers stood in its upper floor, whose timber frame is regular. No signal was put on it, to hide the work. dH = 3.1667 toises.

directions.commission_quote: (72) Pour l'angle à Cullan, la commission a pris le milieu entre les deux dernières séries; il me semble que j'aurois préféré la troisième, qui est la seule dans laquelle le belvédère se vit parfaitement, et qui ne fut pas troublée par le soleil. L'angle seroit plus foible de 0"29. L'angle à Morlac est de toute l'opération celui qui présente le plus de bizarrerie. Par le choix que j'avois cru devoir faire entre les séries, l'erreur de ce triangle étoit seulement de 3"54 ... il n'y a que quelques fractions entre les angles de la commission et les miens, lorsqu'on les corrige pour le calcul, en distribuant l'erreur également entre les trois.

stations.name: Matagalls
stations.occupied: 18 September to 21 October 1792 (dates printed: 18, 19 September; 3, 6, 7, 20, 21 October 1792)
stations.observers: Tranchot (T.), M. Planez (lieutenant de vaisseau, assistant of M. Gonzalez) and M. Chaix (C.), now vice-director of the royal observatory of Madrid
stations.instrument: Circle divided in 360 degrees (sexagesimal); no circle number printed
stations.signal: Signal de Matagall ou de Monsên (station XCIII). A conical tent on the north peak, named Matagall, of Monsên, the largest mountain of south-east Catalonia. The south peak, Homa-Mort, is a little higher.
stations.eccentric: Angles printed as 'observés au centre'; only small 'Excentricité' terms printed (-0.011, -0.072, +0.072). No r or y printed.

stations.occupied: About fifteen days (Méchain: 'j'ai passé quinze jours à Puig-Rodòs'). Dates printed: 10, 11, 13, 14, 15 vendémiaire an premier; 6, 7 and 11 October.

stations.instrument: Repeating circle read in grades; no circle number printed. Telescope 0.6389 toise above the ground.
stations.signal: Signal de Puig-Rodòs (station XCIV), the highest point of a mountain between the village of l'Estan and the town of Moïa, three to four leagues south-west of Vicq. A conical tent, as at the stations before.
stations.eccentric: Angles printed as 'observés au centre'; only small 'Excentricité' terms printed (+0.080, -0.085, +0.006). For Mont-Serrat a reduction to the signal: -3.786 (1st series, sighting the apparent middle of the chapel) and +10.169 (2nd series, sighting the east corner of the chapel).

stations.name: Mont-Serrat
stations.occupied: 14 to 16 October (five to six days at the station; 'pendant les cinq à six jours qu'on a passé ici')
stations.observers: Méchain (M.), with MM. Gonzalez and Alvarez (A.)
stations.instrument: Repeating circle read in grades; no circle number printed. Circle 0.667 toise above the chapel floor.
stations.signal: Signal de Mont-Serrat (station XCVI), on the highest peak near the middle of the summit, near the hermitage of Saint-Gérôme. A long beam fixed against the wall in the middle of the door of the small chapel of Notre-Dame, ending in a small truncated pyramid. Its top was 1.0208 toise above the roof ridge and 2.713 toises above the chapel floor.

stations.name: Montjoui
stations.occupied: Main angle: 27 October 1792 (first series); zenith distances 28 October 1792. Secondary angles and later zenith distances in ventôse an 1, nivôse and ventôse an 2.
stations.instrument: Repeating circle read in grades for the main angle; one later zenith distance (16 ventôse an 1) is printed in sexagesimal degrees. No circle number printed.
stations.signal: Tour de Montjouy (station XCVIII), in the middle of one of the long sides of the barracks of the fort, toward Barcelona. A mast of about twenty feet on the tower platform, used to hoist flags for ships, was the sight point for all the stations that observed this one. The edge of the battlements is 105.096 toises above sea level.
stations.eccentric: Large and different for each series. Matas-Valvidrera: r = 1.5313426 toise, y = 169° 27'7 (1st series, rejected); r = 1.653935, y = 169° 33'6 (2nd series).

directions.commission_note: The special commission rejected the series of 24: poor conditions, it was left out of the observations sent in an 2, and the next series looked very conclusive. The text calls this angle the southern end of the meridian.
directions.dates: 27 October 1792 (series of 24); no date printed for the series of 32
directions.quote: La commission spéciale a rejeté cette série, à cause qu'elle a été faite dans des circonstances peu favorables, qu'on avoit oublié de la comprendre dans l'envoi des observations en l'an 2, et sur-tout parce que la série suivante a paru très-concluante.

gaps: Dunkerque: no calendar dates printed for the Gravelines-Watten series or for the 2nd and 3rd Watten-Cassel series (hours only).
Gravelines: no station register in Tome I. The Tableau des triangles marks its angle in triangle 2 with '*' (concluded, not observed).
Helfaut: no station register in Tome I. Its angles in triangles 4, 5, 9 and 10 are marked '*' in the Tableau (concluded).
Watten: no calendar dates printed for the angle series; only the zenith distances carry dates (25 May to 3 June 1793).
Cassel: triangle 9 angle Helfaut-Béthune (75 53 9.51) is the sum of two observed angles, not a direct series. Page 23 (detail of the tower-axis correction) was not transcribed.
Fiefs: the 'Au centre' line for Bonnières-Sauti is printed 34° 52' 51"66; the minutes are a misprint for 32'.
Béthune: the 'Milieu entre les deux séries' for Cassel-Helfaut is printed 57° 29' 19"65; the degrees are a misprint for 37. Dates printed only for the Fiefs-Mesnil series (28 June 1793).
Béthune: page 37 (theory of placing the circle on the circumscribed circle) was not transcribed; it holds no angle values.
Mesnil: no date printed for the Béthune-Fiefs and Fiefs-Sauti series.
Sauti, Bonnières, Beauquêne, Mailli, Bayonvillers, Villersbreton, Arvillers, Sourdon, Vignacourt, Amiens: many series carry hours but no calendar date; only the dates given in 'occupied' are printed.

Beauquêne: angles 79 40 14.14 (triangle 16) and 65 55 58.56 (triangle 15) are concluded angles ('*' in the Tableau); Villers-Bretonneux could not be seen from Beauquêne, so there is no register series for these two angles.
Amiens: angle Villersbreton-Sourdon 60 31 54.00 (triangle 22) is a concluded angle ('*'); Sourdon cannot be seen from Amiens, so there is no register series.
Beauquêne and Bayonvillers: fractions in the printed heights and dH (Beauquêne 16 and 6 toises 'and a fraction', Bayonvillers dH = 8 and a fraction) are not legible on the scan.
Beauquêne Mailli-Sauti (triangle 14): register 59 3 27.85 (mean of five series); Tableau 59 3 28.53 (commission dropped the first series). The register does not print the four-series reduction.
Vignacourt Villersbreton-Beauquêne (triangle 16): register 65 14 50.65; Tableau 65 14 50.05. No reason for the 0.60 difference is printed.
Arvillers: register 28 11 28.08 (triangle 21) and 67 38 21.17 (triangle 18); Tableau 28 11 28.35 and 67 38 21.22. No reason printed in the register for these differences.
Amiens (triangle 23): the Tableau 'Pages' column prints 70 for the Amiens angle; the angle is on register p. 76.

Les Invalides: no station register in vol. 1; the Tableau marks its angle in triangle 37 as concluded (no page). Its zenith distances from other stations are printed (Dammartin p. 99, Panthéon p. 105, Bellassise p. 118).
Coivrel: the year is not printed on pp. 77-80; only day and month (24 to 27 September).
Clermont: no dates printed for any series (pp. 84-87). Height of the turret above the balustrade has one faint digit (1.4?7 toises).
Clermont, triangle 29 (Coivrel-Saint-Christophe): no direct angle printed; the Tableau value equals the sum of the two horizon angles on p. 86 (CALC).
St.-Martin, triangle 32 (Clermont-Dammartin): no direct angle printed; the Tableau value (pp. 95-97) equals the sum of the two horizon angles on pp. 95 and 97 (CALC).
Dammartin, triangle 32: register horizon value 48 1 54.24 (p. 100); the Tableau prints 48 1 54.53. No reason printed on p. 100 for the 0.29 difference.
Dammartin, triangle 34 (Jonquières-Saint-Martin): no horizon reduction printed on p. 102; the Tableau value 81 18 52.89 does not appear in the register.
St.-Christophe, triangle 31: register horizon 62 36 58.90 (p. 94); Tableau 62 36 58.79, explained by the Tableau note (31) as the commission's value.
St.-Martin, triangle 35: the two reduced values 76 2 29.31 and 76 2 30.28 are reprinted as 76 2 29.08 and 76 2 29.54 on p. 97 without a stated reason.
Panthéon: no reduction to centre printed for the triangle angles; series dates printed only for some series.
Dammartin and Bellassise: most series not dated.
Brie: no calendar date printed for the Bellassise-Panthéon series (p. 124-125); the later series are dated only 'frimaire an 6'.
Brie, triangle 40 (Montlhéri-Tour de Croy): angle not printed. Tableau note (40) says the observations made at Brie for the Croy signal were not printed.
Montlhéri: the identity of observer 'T.' in an 6 is not given on pp. 133-135; no calendar dates printed for the 1792 series.
Malvoisine: no calendar dates printed for the 1792 series (pp. 138-139).
Melun: the register value 63 43 34.08 (p. 144) differs from 63 43 33.79 in the Tableau des triangles (p. 524); no explanation printed at the station.
Lieursaint: p. 146 prints 53° 57' (not 53° 37') in the 'Milieu entre les 80 angles' and 'Horizon' lines for Montlhéri-Malvoisine; kept as printed.
Bruyère: no dates printed for the station (pp. 147-148). The Tableau value 43 49 51.32 is not printed on p. 148 (the page gives 43 49 49.32 or 43 49 51.0).
Torfou: no calendar dates printed. Three Tableau values differ from the register horizon values with no reason printed: triangle 44 (54.79 vs 55.42), 45 (56.52 vs 55.52), 46 (54.00 vs 53.56).
Forêt: no dates printed; observer of the Méréville-Pithiviers series not printed. Tableau prints 57 11 18.00 for triangle 51 against 57 11 18.51 on p. 155; no reason printed.

Chapelle: p. 157 prints 40° 20' 53"32 in the Horizon line of Malvoisine-Forêt (series give 46°). Tableau values differ from the register for triangle 52 (53.92 vs 53.32) and 50 (38.00 vs 37.69); no reason printed at the station.

Pithiviers: last digit of y for Boiscommun-Chapelle (330° 4' 4?") unreadable on p. 162. Observer of Forêt-Méréville not printed. Tableau values differ from the register for triangle 50 (29 55 18.00 vs 29 55 19.00) and 51 (30 40 20.00 vs 30 40 19.73); Tableau gives page 167 for the triangle 53 angle printed on p. 162.
Pithiviers: angles to Orléans and Neuville (pp. 163-164) are not in the Tableau triangles and are not transcribed as directions.
Tour de Croy, St.-Yon, Bromeille, Méréville: no register section; the Tableau marks their angles '*' (concluded from the other two angles). No station entry.
